about: BEUK:notelabels — one table of made-up books for the two copies of the note numbering: the studio's (client/index.html noteBookShown, read by studio/test/note-labels-as-typed.test.ts) and the server's (src/book/notes.ts, read by tests/note-labels.test.ts). `sections` is each section's stored text; `shown` is that text as a reader is shown its notes: every label that is not a number written as the number it takes. Written by hand from the rule, not taken from either copy's output.

cases.name: labels that are no numbers take 1, 2 … in the order they are first marked through the book
sections:
The caravan left[^salt] at dawn.

[^salt]: Salt, by the sack.

The pans lay white[^pans].

[^pans]: The pans of the coast.
shown:
The caravan left[^1] at dawn.

[^1]: Salt, by the sack.

The pans lay white[^2].

[^2]: The pans of the coast.

cases.name: a book of numbers is handed back exactly as stored, whatever order they stand in
sections:
Three[^1] and a bare one.[7]

[^1]: Again from one.
shown:
Three[^1] and a bare one.[7]

[^1]: Again from one.

cases.name: mixed: a number shows as typed, and a named note takes the next number the writer has not used
sections:
One[^1] two[^salt] three[^3] four[^pans].

[^1]: First.

[^salt]: Salt.

[^3]: Third.

[^pans]: Pans.
shown:
One[^1] two[^2] three[^3] four[^4].

[^1]: First.

[^2]: Salt.

[^3]: Third.

[^4]: Pans.

cases.name: mixed across chapters: a number used anywhere in the book is never given to a named note
a label defined in two chapters is two notes, each chapter's own
a label defined twice in one section: a mark means the next definition at or after it, else the last one before
sections:
One[^a] and again[^a].

[^a]: First.

Two[^a].

[^a]: Second.

After the last[^a].
shown:
One[^1] and again[^1].

[^1]: First.

Two[^2].

[^2]: Second.

After the last[^2].

cases.name: a label with punctuation; a label that is a number with leading zeros shows as typed and keeps 7 from every named note
a number of four digits is a label like any other number: it shows as typed
a mark no note answers is numbered once for its label; a later chapter's mark of an earlier chapter's note shows that note's number; a note nothing marks takes its number where it stands
sections:
Dawn[^fn-9] broke[^note] twice[^fn-9], and lost[^nowhere].

[^fn-9]: The first note.

[^note]: The second.

Rain[^fn_3] came, see[^note] and[^nowhere].

[^spare]: Nobody points here.

[^fn_3]: The third note.
shown:
Dawn[^1] broke[^2] twice[^1], and lost[^3].

[^1]: The first note.

[^2]: The second.

Rain[^4] came, see[^2] and[^3].

[^5]: Nobody points here.

[^4]: The third note.

cases.name: a mark inside a note's own text is a mark, numbered where it stands (here the first mark in the text); a definition written before its mark is found
sections:
[^b]: Stands first, see[^a].

Text[^b] here.

[^a]: Marked only from a note.
shown:
[^2]: Stands first, see[^1].

Text[^2] here.

[^1]: Marked only from a note.

cases.name: a log is the writer's to the character; a bare [word] is the writer's word; a bare [12] is a note's number
sections:
Text[^a] and [word] and [12].

::: log
09:14 [^a] raw [^b]
:::

[^a]: A.
shown:
Text[^1] and [word] and [12].

::: log
09:14 [^a] raw [^b]
:::

[^1]: A.

cases.name: a definition on a line of a container is a definition; one set in from the margin in the middle of a paragraph is not
sections:

Ana: Meet me at the pier[^p]
[^p]: The north pier.
:::

[^1]: The north pier.

A line
  [^2]: not a note, and[^2] is marked twice.
